title: Storage
examples: What is the difference between RAM and a hard drive?
Which type of storage is fastest for running programs?
Can you explain how an SSD works compared to an old hard drive?

explain.say: Today we say about computer storage devices. We will learn about different types of memory.
Primary storage is the computer's working memory. It holds data the CPU needs right now. This memory is very fast but loses data when power goes off.
Secondary storage keeps data long term. It keeps files safe even when the power is turned off. Examples include hard drives and SSDs.
Magnetic storage uses magnetism to store bits. Hard disk drives use spinning magnetic platters to write data. This was common in older computers.
Optical storage reads data using lasers. CDs and DVDs use pits and lands on a disc surface. These are read by focusing a light beam.
Solid-state storage uses flash memory chips. SSDs have no moving parts, making them much faster than magnetic drives. They are very reliable.

faq.q: What is the main difference between RAM and SSD?
faq.a: RAM is primary memory used for active tasks and is volatile. An SSD is secondary storage for permanent files and does not need power to keep data.
asks: What kind of memory is RAM?

faq.a: Most traditional hard drives are magnetic. However, newer, smaller drives might use different technologies, but the core principle remains magnetic recording.
asks: What makes a hard drive magnetic?
Does magnetic storage always use spinning parts?

faq.q: Can I use a CD to back up my important photos?
faq.a: You can, but they have limited capacity and are slower to read than modern SSDs. It is better to use a large external solid-state drive.
asks: Are CDs still useful for backup?
What is the capacity of a CD?

faq.q: Why is volatile memory called volatile?
faq.a: It is called volatile because it loses all its stored information when the electrical power supply is removed from the computer.
asks: What does volatile mean in computing?
Does RAM keep data without power?

faq.q: Which storage is best for a modern gaming PC?
faq.a: A combination is best. You need fast RAM for gameplay and an SSD for fast loading times of games and the operating system.
asks: Should I buy an SSD or a big HDD?
What is the best mix of storage?

facts: RAM is primary memory and is volatile.
SSDs use flash memory and have no moving parts.
HDDs store data using magnetic spinning platters.
Optical media like CDs use lasers to read data.

quiz.say: Which type of storage is best for running the operating system for quick startup?
quiz.why: SSDs are solid-state and have no moving parts, making them much faster for loading the operating system than mechanical drives.

wrong.0: Although RAM is very fast, it is primary memory and is designed for active programs, not long-term OS storage.
wrong.1: HDDs use spinning magnetic platters, which introduces mechanical delays that slow down the startup process.
wrong.2: Optical discs are designed for reading and are significantly slower than modern solid-state drives.

quiz.say: If you lose power suddenly, which type of memory will lose all its data?
quiz.why: RAM is volatile memory, meaning its electrical charge that holds data dissipates when the power is cut.

wrong.0: Optical discs are physical media and retain their data regardless of power loss.
wrong.2: SSDs use flash memory, which retains data even when the power is removed.
wrong.3: HDDs are also non-volatile; the magnetic data remains on the platters.

quiz.say: Which storage method relies on magnetism for data storage?
quiz.why: HDDs work by magnetizing tiny areas on spinning metal platters to represent bits of data.

wrong.0: RAM stores data using electrical charges in capacitors, not magnetic fields.
wrong.2: SSDs store data using electrical charges trapped in flash memory cells, not magnetism.
wrong.3: Optical discs use physical pits and lands read by a laser beam.
